originality.rationale: Main published model analyzes equilibria and multistability; it does not establish uniform global upper-cost selection or every-interior-orbit convergence. Previous risk-fiber invariant-measure theorem excludes interior recurrence in some regions but does not control global boundary selection. The original global argument constructs a risk lower barrier and an exact forced log-odds difference, and provides exact examples showing coexistence and a benefit-side sharpness boundary. Broader unnoticed coverage is possible, especially in an inaccessible PDF supplement.
residual_risks: The 28.4 MB supplementary PDF of the 2026 primary article was not fully inspected; a stronger theorem there could supersede the global claim.
Further general persistence/global attraction theorems for monotone feedback systems might entail a special-case conclusion despite different terminology.
There is no independent mathematical validation.

source_inspections.assessment: The main article lists equilibrium local stability and numerical basins but does not prove a global open-box cost-boundary selection theorem or exponential convergence in the stated strict feedback regime. Supplementary PDF not fully read.

value.rationale: Distinguishes mere existence of nonzero-cooperation stationary points from their dynamic accessibility under feedback, yields a global all-interior basin criterion with rates, and shows through exact examples both hidden positive equilibria despite collapse and genuinely attracting cooperation when the benefit bound is relaxed. This answers a motivated governance dynamical-systems question absent from source equilibrium census.
